text:
sara: noticed a cluster-level increase in GPU attach failures in eu-west1, correlated with a spike in local NVMe write amplification. here's a log sample, looks like write frontier got truncated -> silent corruption? :eyes:

ops-bot: alert created: NVMeWriteAmp-EUW1 - affected 23 hosts, severity: high

james: can you paste the dmesg+nvme logs from one of the affected nodes? is this correlated with nightly model rollout?

sara: paste below from gnode-eu-134:
```
[1703056700.123] nvme0n1: io 12345 error, submitted: 4096, returned: 0
[1703056700.125] overlayfs: lowerdir writeback truncation at offset 2147483648
[1703056700.130] scrubber: write amplification ratio=5.8, scheduled rate 120MB/s
[1703056721.001] gpu-provisioner: attach failed: device missing mapping
```

mike: looks like overlayfs writeback + truncated block map. we saw similar once with a kernel regression on the fscache path. what kernel is running?

james: kernel 5.10.153-rt. Was there a recent kernel or nvme firmware push to eu-west1?

sara: firmware push 2026-02-11 rolled to eu-west1 at 02:00 UTC. rollout batch size 50. first errors ~02:12. other regions green.

anya: brief cost note: if this is firmware causing higher write amplification we can either increase spare overprovisioning (buy more drives / reduce usable capacity) or throttle janitor + scrubber to reduce IO. former is capex, latter is operational cost (SLO risk).

leo: +1 to throttling as short term. but if drive FW is degrading wear, spares will save replacements. estimate: replacing 100 drives ~ $40k, overprovisioning by 7% across pool ~ $10k annual capacity hit.

james: for mitigation, can we flip janitor window to night-only and reduce concurrent scrub threads on affected hosts? also enable per-host IO cgroups for scrubber service.

sara: will run a canary: pause firmware for next batch, reduce scrub threads to 2 on affected hosts, set scrubber rate limit to 40MB/s. scheduling a canary on 10 hosts now.

mike: if overlayfs is involved consider turning on "sync_lowpri_writes=1" and set dm-writecache off for the canary to avoid metadata racing. command to set temporarily:
```bash
# sysctl change for canary hosts
sysctl -w fs.overlay.sync_lowpri_writes=1
systemctl restart scrubber.service
```

james: also open a firmware rollback play if canary fails. @oncall please standby. :rotating_light:

sara: opened runbook stub and ticket #INF-4832, will document steps and outcomes. copying short run steps:
- pause firmware rollout for eu-west1
- set scrubber_rate_mb=40 and scrub_threads=2 on affected hosts
- toggle sysctl overlay sync_lowpri_writes=1
- monitor attach failures and nvme write amplification ratio for 30m

janitor-bot: ticket INF-4832 created and assigned to sara, priority P1

anya: re: economics, if we expect this to reoccur under heavy write workloads (batch model builds) we should evaluate moving some GPU fleets to ephemeral SSDs with firmware vetted for low WA. that increases hourly fleet cost ~8% but reduces replacement churn.

leo: create spreadsheet with replacement vs capacity loss vs hourly cost tradeoffs, I'll model a 12-month TCO.

sara: canary running now (10 hosts). I'll post results in 30m. thanks all.
